question.text: A Cat III AIF's listed mid-cap long position (5% of NAV) is suspended by the exchange following a forensic-audit announcement; resumption is uncertain for 90+ days. The CIO receives new subscription requests next week. What is the MOST APPROPRIATE action for the Investment Manager?

answer.text: Continue marking the suspended stock at last traded price and accept new subscriptions at current NAV
Segregate the suspended position into a side-pocket (separate class) so new subscriptions and redemptions interact only with the main NAV, protecting all parties
Write the position off to zero immediately
Pause ALL fund operations until resumption

explanation.text: The Logic: A suspended listed position with uncertain resumption cannot be marked reliably at the last traded price, because that price no longer represents fair value. Segregating it into a side-pocket (a separate class) means existing unitholders retain their proportionate share of the suspended position's eventual upside or downside, new subscriptions interact only with the main NAV (so they do not free-ride on a potential recovery), and the unreliable mark does not contaminate ongoing daily NAVs. Writing the position to zero or pausing all fund operations are disproportionate responses. The Trap: Option A allows new subscribers to buy at a stale mark — economically unfair. Option C pre-empts a possible recovery by impairing to zero. Option D suspends activity the fund has no operational basis to suspend. Note: Side-pocket segregation for a suspended listed position and the free-riding mechanics described above are not explicitly set out in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which support fair-value methods for liquid/illiquid securities, valuation-policy disclosure, independent valuation, and suspension of redemptions/new subscriptions in exceptional circumstances. The side-pocket framing reflects general industry practice for handling illiquid/suspended holdings in pooled funds.
